title: The printing press (c. 1455)
hook: Gutenberg's first great book is the Bible

segments.voice: Yesterday, Catherine of Genoa, who nursed the sick and called purgatorium love's fire. Your line was love burns clean.

Ink and oil: that's the smell of this workshop in Mainz. A man leans on the bar of a wooden press, and a sheet comes up wet with black letters in neat columns. Then another sheet, with the same letters in the same places. Then another. Until now, in Europe, a Bible came into the world by a scribe's long labor, one letter at a time. Here the same page is coming off a machine, again and again. The man in charge is Johannes Gutenberg, and the book on his press is the Bible.
screen: `INK AND OIL IN MAINZ.` → `THE SAME PAGE, AGAIN AND AGAIN.` → `THE BOOK ON THE PRESS: THE BIBLE.`

segments.voice: Start with the trick. Gutenberg's press used movable type: small metal letters, cast so they could be set into lines, inked, pressed, then taken apart and used again. Next, the book he chose: the Bible in Latin, the Vulgate, the translation the Church read at Mass. It was printed in dark, handsome letters made to look like a scribe's best work. Often the colored initials and decorations were added by hand afterward, so no two copies looked quite alike. Then, what changed. A text copied by hand could drift a little with each copy. A printed page stayed the same from one copy to the next. More people could own books, compare them, and read for themselves. In the years ahead, Catholics and Protestants alike would put presses to work, and that story is coming. Finally, the reason for thanks. The psalm says, in the Douay-Rheims, "Thy word is a lamp to my feet, and a light to my paths." Before Mainz, in Europe, that lamp was copied by hand. Now a machine could make it page after page, for many more hands. Your line today calls it the first book printed. That's how the story is sometimes told. Historians would add that printing is older than Gutenberg, and that his Bible is the great book his press is remembered for.
screen: `MOVABLE METAL TYPE.` · `THE BIBLE IN LATIN, THE VULGATE.` · `THE SAME PAGE IN EVERY COPY.` · `THY WORD IS A LAMP TO MY FEET.` · then, large: `THE FIRST BOOK PRINTED.`

segments.voice: Reach for one printed thing near you, a Bible, a prayer card, a cookbook with someone's notes in the margin, and feel its weight. Think of the hands behind it: the writer, the translator, the typesetter, the printer, the person who gave it to you. If you pray, thank God for each of them, or pray the psalm's line, thy word is a lamp to my feet; if not, thank them one by one.
Gutenberg. The craftsman in Mainz whose movable metal type printed the Latin Bible again and again, the same from one copy to the next. Today's word.
Your line: the first book printed. The week ran from Bridget and the Modern Devotion to Joan, Rita, Brother Klaus, purgatorium, and the press. Seven days, done; see you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics read printed Scripture at Mass from the lectionary and the Book of the Gospels, and some keep a printed Bible, missal or prayer book at home for daily prayer.

chat.says: Why does Gutenberg's printing press matter so much in Church history?
options: Movable type made the same Bible page again and again, so many more could own and read it.
He invented writing for Europe; before him, almost no books existed at all.
He printed the first Bible in plain German so ordinary people could read it.

notes: Index carry 'the first book printed' is kept exactly but is historically loose: printing (including movable type) existed in East Asia before Gutenberg, and Gutenberg's shop printed smaller items before the Bible. The teach says so gently ('printing is older than Gutenberg'). Suggest an owner-approved index change, e.g. 'the first great printed book'.
Confirm Douay-Rheims (Challoner) wording of Psalm 118:105 and John 1:1.
